01 / THE UNION+

Big questions.
Better together.

Purdue Computer Pioneer Union brings people together to explore the ideas shaping the next era of computing.

We discuss what’s happening in computing, from new research and industry news to product launches and the tools people are using. We share articles, try out new technology, and learn from each other’s projects. Bring something you’ve read, something you’re working on, or a question you’d like to talk through.

Find your next rabbit hole Meet the people
02 / FIELD NOTES+

From the frontier.
Into the conversation.

Research worth a closer look.
New papers. Critical readings. Open questions.

01HARDWARE / SOFTWARE
FlashAttention-4 · March 2026

FlashAttention-4 Finds the Work Faster GPUs Leave Behind

Blackwell makes matrix multiplication faster, but attention still has other work to do. FlashAttention-4 shows why the next performance gain can come from scheduling, exponentials, and moving less data.

4 min readRead the analysis
02HYPOTHESIS / EXPERIMENT
R&D-Agent-Quant · NeurIPS 2025

When a Quant Agent Can Rewrite Its Own Experiment

R&D-Agent-Quant links financial hypotheses, executable code, and backtest feedback. Its most interesting contribution is a research loop we can inspect, along with new reasons to protect the evaluation.

4 min readRead the analysis
03LANGUAGE / ACTION
π0.7 · April 2026

π0.7 and the Difference a Robot Coach Makes

Physical Intelligence’s π0.7 uses richer prompts to combine diverse robot experience. Its appliance experiments suggest a practical route to new skills, but coaching and unaided generalization need separate scorecards.

4 min readRead the analysis
04SIMULATION / REALITY
Waymo World Model · February 2026

Waymo’s World Model Turns “What If?” into a Test

Waymo’s World Model generates camera and lidar scenes that respond to driving actions. That opens useful counterfactual tests, while raising a harder question: how do we validate the simulated world?

4 min readRead the analysis
05ASSISTANCE / UNDERSTANDING
AI tutoring trial · October 2026

An AI Tutor Trial Shows Why the Study Routine Matters

A new university trial makes AI tutoring harder to summarize in a headline. Its most useful result concerns how access to an assistant can change the rest of studying.

5 min readRead the analysis
06PERCEPTION / REASONING
AMIE (Video) · August 2026

AMIE’s Video Study Tests More Than Medical Answers

AMIE’s video-consultation study makes a systems problem visible: conversation cannot stop whenever reasoning gets difficult. The architecture is interesting, but its simulated clinical evaluation sets clear limits on the claim.

5 min readRead the analysis
07CONCEPT / PIXEL
SAM 3 · ICLR 2026

SAM 3 and the Problem of Finding Every Match

SAM 3 turns a short concept prompt into masks for matching objects across images and video. Its most revealing test may be a prompt whose answer should be empty.

5 min readRead the analysis
AN EVOLVING RESEARCH FEED

These are our current readings, not the limits of our interests. Each note connects a concrete piece of research with our interpretation, its limits, and a question worth bringing to the room.
